Independent replay: at b=sigma=1, integrate exp(-u) phi_{sqrt(1+2u)}(a) over u>=0 and bracket the zero of this integral minus phi_1(a) in [1,2]. Direct quadrature and root finding give a_c=1.300922293201194, residual 2.776e-17.
correctness.rationale: Here a is half the center-to-center separation. At equilibrium the exponential reset age gives displacement transform 1/(1+b^2 k^2); any two initial laws couple at the first reset, so this invariant law is unique. The one-component profile g_b solves the Gaussian-forced resolvent equation. Its ratio to the width-sigma Gaussian is strictly increasing on x>0 by the positive mixture of strictly wider Gaussians, starts below one and tends to infinity. The curvature at sigma is strictly negative termwise, so the crossing is beyond sigma. Differentiating the resolvent gives g_b'''(a_c)>0 and g_b''''(a_c)=-phi_sigma''(a_c)/b^2<0. The derivative of the equal Laplace mixture changes signs exactly at -a, 0, a; Gaussian damping converts its convolution into a bilateral exponential transform. Differentiation after multiplication by an exponential multiplies the measure by y-c at a sign boundary c, removing one sign change. Analyticity and Rolle with multiplicities inductively give at most three real zeros. The origin, symmetry and the strict negative derivative at x=a for a>0 then establish all regimes, with the critical cubic derivative zero exhausting the count. Applying the implicit-function theorem in x^2 gives the claimed coefficient and O((a-a_c)^(3/2)) remainder. For small b the curvature expansion uses the second and fourth Laplace moments and the nonzero Gaussian curvature slope at sigma; for large b, the two-sided Laplace expectation bound at the crossing first gives a_c=O(sigma sqrt(log(b/sigma))), then the stated logarithmic constant. These arguments cover all fixed positive b and sigma, including a=0, but not r=0.
residual_risks: Quadrature corroborates one case only; the analytical proof carries the global and limiting assertions.

value.rationale: An invariant density formula alone does not tell whether reset-location bimodality is visible after diffusion. The sharp global transition excludes extra stationary points, separates reset bimodality from stationary bimodality, and describes the scale needed to retain peaks under infrequent resetting. The critical opening coefficient and endpoint laws quantify this distinction without making finite-sample or other-kernel claims.
residual_risks: The value is a theorem for this symmetric equal-variance free model, not a claim about arbitrary reset distributions or empirical observability.
